react_result.final_narrative_text: The ten differentially abundant metabolites converge on two interconnected amino-acid and one-carbon metabolic hubs. Glycine, serine, threonine, and cysteine are the dominant drivers: they rank as the top pathway hit in both the RaMP multi-database ORA (FDR 8.6×10⁻¹⁷) and the mummichog m/z-direct analysis (p=0.0029), and appear again in MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA as the second-ranked pathway (KEGG:hsa00260, p=3.3×10⁻⁷). The same four amino acids together with S-adenosylmethionine and adenosine score the one-carbon pool by folate pathway (KEGG:hsa00670) as the single most significant result in MetaboAnalystR (p=8.4×10⁻¹⁰) and as the RaMP ORA top hit (FDR 8.4×10⁻¹⁰), reflecting the folate-mediated interconversion of serine, glycine and one-carbon units. Methionine and cysteine metabolism (KEGG:hsa00270 / MUMM:methionine_and_cysteine_metabolism) is the third cross-paradigm winner, enriched in all three tools (p=6×10⁻⁴ to 1.1×10⁻¹⁴), anchored by S-adenosylmethionine, L-cysteine, L-serine and adenosine. Choline (C00114) is a shared member of the glycine/serine cluster and the glycerophospholipid metabolism pathway hit by mummichog, consistent with its role in methyl-group donation upstream of SAM. 3,4-Dihydroxyphenylacetaldehyde (C04043) uniquely anchors the tyrosine metabolism branch (mummichog p=0.050), pointing to catecholamine oxidative metabolism as a secondary perturbation. The cross-paradigm convergence on glycine–serine–threonine metabolism and one-carbon folate cycling indicates a treatment-induced rebalancing of amino-acid catabolism and methyl-group availability.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-analysis tools (RaMP multi-database ORA, MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA, and mummichog m/z-direct analysis) consistently identify amino-acid and one-carbon metabolism as the dominant perturbation. RaMP ORA ranks KEGG:map00260 "Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism" as the top hit (FDR 8.6×10⁻¹⁷, 737-fold enrichment, 7 of 10 input metabolites hit including glycine, L-serine, L-threonine, L-cysteine, choline, adenosine, and S-adenosylmethionine). MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently confirms this same pathway at rank 1 (p = 3.3×10⁻⁷) and places KEGG:hsa00670 "One-carbon pool by folate" at the top rank (p = 8.4×10⁻¹⁰, 6 metabolites hit: glycine, S-adenosylmethionine, choline, L-serine, adenosine, L-cysteine). The mummichog m/z-direct network analysis reproduces the amino-acid hub as top-ranked (p = 0.003) and adds a second convergent pathway, MUMM:methionine_and_cysteine_metabolism (p = 0.0098), which also appears at rank 2 in MetaboAnalystR (KEGG:hsa00270, p = 6×10⁻⁴). Glycerophospholipid metabolism (p = 0.028) and tyrosine metabolism (p = 0.051) emerge as secondary mummichog-specific hits not reaching the top-5 in RaMP or MetaboAnalystR. Across all tools, the five driver metabolites are glycine, L-serine, S-adenosylmethionine, L-cysteine, and choline, which collectively bridge the folate one-carbon cycle and the transsulfuration pathway through shared methyl-donor and amino-acid interconversion chemistry.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: The ten differentially abundant metabolites converge on two interconnected amino-acid and one-carbon metabolic hubs. Glycine, serine, threonine, and cysteine are the dominant drivers: they rank as the top pathway hit in both the RaMP multi-database ORA (FDR 8.6×10⁻¹⁷) and the mummichog m/z-direct analysis (p=0.0029), and appear again in MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA as the second-ranked pathway (KEGG:hsa00260, p=3.3×10⁻⁷). The same four amino acids together with S-adenosylmethionine and adenosine score the one-carbon pool by folate pathway (KEGG:hsa00670) as the single most significant result in MetaboAnalystR (p=8.4×10⁻¹⁰) and as the RaMP ORA top hit (FDR 8.4×10⁻¹⁰), reflecting the folate-mediated interconversion of serine, glycine and one-carbon units. Methionine and cysteine metabolism (KEGG:hsa00270 / MUMM:methionine_and_cysteine_metabolism) is the third cross-paradigm winner, enriched in all three tools (p=6×10⁻⁴ to 1.1×10⁻¹⁴), anchored by S-adenosylmethionine, L-cysteine, L-serine and adenosine. Choline (C00114) is a shared member of the glycine/serine cluster and the glycerophospholipid metabolism pathway hit by mummichog, consistent with its role in methyl-group donation upstream of SAM. 3,4-Dihydroxyphenylacetaldehyde (C04043) uniquely anchors the tyrosine metabolism branch (mummichog p=0.050), pointing to catecholamine oxidative metabolism as a secondary perturbation. The cross-paradigm convergence on glycine–serine–threonine metabolism and one-carbon folate cycling indicates a treatment-induced rebalancing of amino-acid catabolism and methyl-group availability.
